answer: Each agent publishes a signed proof of work tied to a transient zephyr‑seeded challenge; the challenge hash is stored in an opal‑colored ledger entry at the network wharf. When a new node registers, it must solve the challenge and also answer a randomly injected honeypot query that only legitimate agents can decode; colluding Sybil bots fail the query and are flagged. The cost to the attacker grows linearly with each fake identity, because every node requires a fresh proof‑of‑work and a unique honeypot answer, turning a cheap flood into a computationally expensive campaign.
